goal: On desktop the owner reaches every dashboard sub-route from sidebar children and sees no in-page pill bar; on mobile every one of those sub-routes stays reachable exactly as it is today, and the Review QR surface lives under Requests instead of Settings.
non_goals: Deleting ReviewsTabs, RequestsTabs or AnalyticsTabs — #1089 reversed that; they are retained and scoped to mobile
Moving or changing the QR redirect GET /q/[businessId] — printed codes point at it
Changing which locations are QR-eligible, or the subscriptionAllowsQrRedirect gate
Adding a children row to MobileTabBar — #1089 chose the pill bar for mobile instead
Deleting the shared .tabs/.tab styles — CardViewTabs is a view switch and keeps them
Changing the solicitation feature flag's meaning or default
user_visible_behavior: Above 768px the Reviews, Requests and Analytics pages render no pill tab bar.
The sidebar lists Needs Action and All Reviews under Reviews, Contacts and Review QR under Requests, and Metrics and Restraint under Analytics.
At or below 768px each of those pages still renders its pill bar, and Requests gains a third pill for Review QR.
The Review QR surface answers at /dashboard/requests/qr, and its printable per-location view at /dashboard/requests/qr/print/[businessId].
An owner opening the old /settings/review-qr URL is redirected to the new one rather than seeing a 404.
The Settings sidebar no longer lists Review QR.
When solicitation is disabled, Review QR appears as a top-level sidebar row and in the mobile tab bar's Requests slot, so every owner can still reach it.
On a section whose first child shares the parent's route, only the child is announced as the current page; the parent keeps its open-section styling.
The Reviews sidebar child reads 'Needs Action', matching the tab it opens (previously 'Needs action').
The old /settings/review-qr/print/[businessId] path redirects to the moved printable view instead of 404ing.
invariants: Every sub-route reachable on a phone today stays reachable on a phone after this change.
deriveNavSection remains the single owner of the nav-highlight rule; Sidebar and MobileTabBar both read it and cannot drift.
The QR redirect GET /q/[businessId] and src/lib/locations/review-qr.ts are untouched, so printed Review QR codes keep resolving.
The Requests section and all of its children stay hidden when the solicitation flag is off.
Exactly one nav row highlights for any pathname.
The 768px boundary is read from the existing console.css rule, never re-spelled as a second number.
edge_cases: Solicitation flag off: the Requests parent and its three children, Review QR included, are all absent.
A pathname under the moved QR route folds to the requests nav section, not to the dashboard catch-all.
The bare /settings pathname still highlights the SETTINGS_DEFAULT_HREF row, which is unrelated to this change.
An owner on the aggregate location scope still reaches Review QR; the surface itself decides eligibility.
A QR-ineligible location still gets its explanatory card, not a dead-end QR.
ContactsClient and ReviewsContent each render their pill bar in two branches; both branches must behave the same.

src/components/dashboard/shell/active-nav.ts deriveNavSection — ordered prefix tests, specific before the catch-all

rollback_plan: Revert the squash commit. No migration, no schema, no flag change and no external state, so a revert fully restores the previous navigation; printed Review QR codes are unaffected either way because GET /q/[businessId] never moves.
